newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London and Paris stocks boosted by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London and Paris stocks boosted by Wall St.

text.p: Stocks in London and Paris climbed on Thursday with trading boosted by a strong close on Wall Street and merger activity but Frankfurt slipped.

On currency markets, the dollar lost some of its early gains against the mark but remained stronger against the yen after Tokyo shares tumbled overnight to their low of the year amid deepening gloom about Japan's economic outlook.
In much of Europe, the mood was undepinned by the buoyancy in New York after bourses on both sides of the Atlantic rose in pre-Christmas holiday business on Wednesday.
The Dow Jones industrial average put on another 38 points overnight to 6,346 in an end-of-year rush to snap up technology stocks, adding to Tuesday's 40 point rally.
London climbed 0.3 percent with trading stimulated by bids and share buybacks in the market which have totalled 2.5 billion pounds ($4.2 billion) in the last two days. But sentiment was restrained.
"The mood is not euphoric today but I can't see why anyone would want to be agressively selling this side of Christmas," said one dealer.
"If we move higher, it will be because of a squeeze on selective stocks, I can't see people making too many adjustments now."
Paris moved ahead 0.7 percent, the best showing of the morning in Europe. The market was cheered by New York and a flurry of merger-related announcements in the pharmaceuticals and retail sectors.
Elf Aquitaine and Sanofi rose strongly after Elf said it would be desirable for its pharmaceutical unit Sanofi to merge with other laboratories to boost profitability.
Rhone-Poulenc climbed 0.6 percent to 167 francs. The drugs group is merging its animal health business with Merck to create a venture with 8.5 billion francs ($1.6 billion) in annual sales.
In Frankfurt, stocks fell as the policy-making council of the Bundesbank met and decided to leave interest rates unchanged. By mid-morning the DAX index had registed a loss of 0.5 percent.
On the currency front, the dollar was stronger after the sharp drop in Japanese stocks and because of a degree of uncertainty over German interest rates.
The yen weakened as a 2.6 percent drop in the Nikkei 225 index of Japanese stocks overnight was seen arguing for Japanese interest rates to remain at record lows for now.
Though the Bunsesbank left rates steady some traders said an outside chance remained that the bank would fix its key securities repurchase rate slightly lower over the year-end holiday period.
The U.S. currency climbed to 1.5583 marks at one stage before slipping back but remained above the level of 1.5541 in late trade on Wednesday.
The Swiss franc was lower in Europe, meantime, and set a two-year low at 1.3372 per dollar and a three-year low at 85.82 centimes per mark at one point.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5555 marks and 113.98 yen, compared with 1.5541 and 113.65 in late business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 12.3 points at 4,030.5.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX was 13.00 lower at 2,807.75.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 16.45 at 2,235.34.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $369.60 an ounce, compared to Wednesday's close of $369.10. Silver was at $4.87, up one cent.
